subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Must OpenClaw’s supported masked-credential guarantee keep raw values outside the OpenClaw and agent subprocess address spaces, or is same-process scoped injection an accepted security tier?
rationale: Current SecretRefs and plugin hooks support same-process injection and defense-in-depth redaction, but they cannot provide the requested guarantee that a compromised agent execution path never accesses raw credentials.

options.title: Capability broker boundary
options.body: Require the strong supported tier to proxy, sign, or dispatch scoped operations without returning raw credentials to OpenClaw or agent-controlled subprocesses.

options.title: Two documented tiers
options.body: Add a strong external broker tier and retain same-process scoped injection as a clearly labeled lower-isolation compatibility option.

options.title: Same-process injection only
options.body: Standardize the current exec-environment hook and redaction model while explicitly declining a raw-secret isolation guarantee.

recommendation.title: Capability broker boundary
recommendation.body: Require the strong supported tier to proxy, sign, or dispatch scoped operations without returning raw credentials to OpenClaw or agent-controlled subprocesses.
